solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Location of hotel in backwoods? (6,2,7)

blocks.note: hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet; find the word that means no place at all and see where its H sits
remote country far from any town

annotation.surface: Someone asking where a hotel is hidden away out in the wilds.
annotation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: take "hotel" as the letter H and ask where it sits in the word NOWHERE. It sits right in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom for a remote spot far from towns is the middle of nowhere, and the H of NOWHERE is its middle letter.

entries.clue: Dinner for one with Tango in tin? (5)

indicatorNotes.in: T goes in the middle of MEAL

blocks.note: dinner is one kind of meal
Tango is T in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A solo supper eaten straight out of a can.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dinner for one" suggests a lonely meal; here "for one" says dinner is one example of a MEAL. The question mark marks tin as one example of a metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the soft silvery element Sn is one metal among many, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: National icon with a mind in flux (9)

indicatorNotes.in flux: things in flux are shifting, so the letters move around

blocks.note: used as it is
used as it is

annotation.surface: A national hero whose thinking keeps changing.
annotation.walkthrough: "National icon" looks like one phrase, but National is the definition on its own, used as a noun: a citizen of a country.
annotation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Dominican Republic or of Dominica is called a Dominican, so the noun fits someone of that nationality.

entries.clue: Song cover cut by ELO originally (4)

indicatorNotes.cut by: the E cuts into the lid, splitting it
indicatorNotes.originally: only the first letter of ELO is used

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
the first letter of ELO

annotation.surface: A cover version of a song trimmed by the band ELO.
annotation.walkthrough: ELO are the Electric Light Orchestra, a 1970s rock band, so "song cover" reads as a cover version.
annotation.definitionFit: A lied is a German art song, as by Schubert.

entries.clue: Head-turning drinks choices (7)

indicatorNotes.Head-turning: the head of the word, its first two letters, turns round

blocks.note: potions are drinks

annotation.surface: Eye-catching drinks on a menu.
annotation.walkthrough: "Head-turning" looks like praise for striking drinks; here the head is the word's first two letters, which turn round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the alternatives open to you when you pick are your options.

entries.clue: New darts channel? (7)

blocks.note: N is short for new
arrows is the players' word for darts

annotation.surface: A new television channel showing darts.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sports TV channel; a channel here is a strip of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrows is a narrow channel of water between two larger ones.

entries.clue: Scornful fan winger hit … (9)

indicatorNotes.fan: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: used as it is

annotation.surface: A scornful supporter hitting a wide player.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fan" looks like a football supporter to go with the winger; it is the instruction to spread the letters out.
annotation.definitionFit: A withering look is one meant to shrivel its target with contempt.

entries.clue: … heading out of home ground (5)

indicatorNotes.heading out of: the head, the first letter, goes out of the word

blocks.note: the hearth stands for home, as in hearth and home

annotation.surface: The winger from the previous clue leaves the home stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots join this to 6D so the two read as one football story; "home ground" is a stadium, but ground is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: earth is the soil underfoot, as in digging the earth.

entries.clue: The ability to survive is an explorer’s craft (9)

blocks.note: the power to last through hardship
craft means a boat here: think of Ernest Shackleton's Antarctic ship

annotation.surface: Survival is the skill an explorer really needs.
annotation.walkthrough: "Craft" reads as a skill; it is a boat. Shackleton's Endurance was crushed by ice in 1915 and all its crew survived.
annotation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going and survive.

entries.clue: Locums ringing English head on the blower (7)

indicatorNotes.ringing: TEMPS form a ring round E
indicatorNotes.head: only the head, the first letter, of "the" is used
indicatorNotes.on: the T comes on after the rest

blocks.note: locums are temps, stand-in workers
E is short for English
the first letter of the

annotation.surface: Stand-in staff phoning round an English boss.
annotation.walkthrough: "On the blower" is British slang for on the phone, so the surface is a phone call; blower is really a wind, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, something that blows hard.

entries.clue: Embarrassed about fatigue in bed? (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so RED is placed around TIRE

blocks.note: red in the face, embarrassed
to fatigue is to tire

annotation.surface: Someone blushing about how tired they are once in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that retired means gone to bed, not stopped working.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night is in bed.

entries.clue: Course porky nurses finish for luncheon (4)

indicatorNotes.nurses: LIE holds the N as a nurse holds a baby

blocks.note: porky is rhyming slang for a lie, from pork pie
the last letter of luncheon

annotation.surface: A plump person taking the last of lunch on a course, perhaps a golf course.
annotation.walkthrough: Porky is British rhyming slang: pork pie = lie. Course is the definition, a line of action.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a direction taken, as in a line of attack or a line of action.

entries.clue: Match court (2,8)

blocks.note: a verb: to suit each other, like colours that pair well
a verb: to date someone, in an old-fashioned phrase

annotation.surface: A court where a match is played, tennis perhaps.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like tennis nouns; both are verbs here.
annotation.definitionFit: Colours that match go together, and courting couples go together too.

entries.clue: Does a runner’s pace upset opponents? (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters of 'S PACE are upset into a new order

blocks.note: East and South, opponents at the bridge table
the letters S, P, A, C, E rearranged

annotation.surface: Asking whether an athlete's speed unsettles the rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition ends mid-word: "Does a runner" stops before the 's, which belongs to the fodder. To do a runner is British slang for running off.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who does a runner escapes, running off without paying.

entries.clue: Lovable rogue in danger with drug (9)

indicatorNotes.rogue: letters gone rogue break out of line

blocks.note: used as it is
E is ecstasy, the drug

annotation.surface: A charming scoundrel in trouble over drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lovable rogue" is a stock phrase, but rogue is the anagram signal and Lovable stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something endearing wins affection, which makes it easy to love.

entries.clue: It’s a job being drunk mostly, right? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is the person who does the job

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, the last letter dropped

blocks.note: plastered, slang for drunk, without its D
R is short for right

annotation.surface: Asking whether being drunk at work counts as a job.
annotation.walkthrough: Plastered means drunk, and a plasterer's job is to plaster walls, which joins the two senses.
annotation.definitionFit: Plasterer is a job, the tradesperson who plasters walls.

entries.clue: Second glove taken by someone (7)

blocks.note: S is short for second
a mitten is a glove

annotation.surface: A second glove picked up by a stranger.
annotation.walkthrough: "Taken by someone" reads as stolen; it means attracted to them.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom match: to be smitten is to be struck with love for a person, and being taken with them means the same.

entries.clue: Ecstasy in freight vehicles (9)

blocks.note: rapture, a state of being carried away with joy
lorries and vans as a group, the means of carrying goods

annotation.surface: Drugs smuggled in lorries.
annotation.walkthrough: Ecstasy looks like the drug (E, as in 13D); it is rapture.
annotation.definitionFit: Transport is overwhelming joy, as in transports of delight.

entries.clue: London bassist’s inside a foreign area (7)

indicatorNotes.inside: the answer lies inside the words

blocks.note: lonDON BASSist's

annotation.surface: Something inside a London bass player, abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: Donbass is the coal-mining region of eastern Ukraine, also spelt Donbas.
annotation.definitionFit: The Donbass is an area in eastern Ukraine, foreign to a British solver.

entries.clue: Small bottle left by a whip (7)

indicatorNotes.left by: the A is left out of the word

blocks.note: S is short for small
bottle is British slang for courage; its A goes
the A that is dropped

annotation.surface: A little bottle left next to a whip.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottle here is nerve: to lose your bottle is to lose your courage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scourge is a lash used for flogging, and the verb sense of punishing grew from it.

entries.clue: One for whom the present is not enough? (7)

annotation.definition: One for whom the present is not enough?

blocks.clueFragment: One for whom the present is not enough
blocks.note: the surface suggests someone restless with the here and now; the setter means someone a gift fails to satisfy
a gift, not the present moment

annotation.surface: A philosopher always living for the future, never content with now.
annotation.walkthrough: "The present" reads as the here and now; it is a gift that fails to please.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingrate shows no thanks for kindness or gifts, so a present never satisfies them.

entries.clue: People shortly to corral horse (7)

indicatorNotes.to corral: IN A BIT pens the H as a corral pens horses

blocks.note: in a bit means shortly
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

annotation.surface: Folk about to round up a horse.
annotation.walkthrough: People is a verb here, meaning to fill with people; H stands for heroin, whose slang name is horse.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to fill a place with residents, to live in it, which is what inhabit means.

entries.clue: Odd shape or top mark (10)

indicatorNotes.Odd: the letters take an odd new shape

blocks.note: used as it is

annotation.surface: A strange shape or the highest score.
annotation.walkthrough: "Top mark" reads as full marks; top belongs to the fodder, and mark alone is the definition, though the setter clearly enjoys that it sits up top.
annotation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark placed high on the line.

entries.clue: Where spring is over in its current form (5)

blocks.note: O is short for over in cricket scoring
as is means in its current state

annotation.surface: Spring is over, as seasons go, just as things now stand.
annotation.walkthrough: Spring reads as the season; it is a water spring in the desert.
annotation.definitionFit: An oasis is a place in the desert where a spring rises.

entries.clue: Tyrant famous soprano knocked back (4)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: the S is knocked one place further back

blocks.note: a star is famous
S is short for soprano; it names the S of STAR as the letter that moves

annotation.surface: A dictator slapping down a celebrated singer.
annotation.walkthrough: In STAR, meaning famous, the S for soprano moves back behind the T.
annotation.definitionFit: The Russian emperors held absolute power, so a tsar is a byword for a despot.

entries.clue: Turns broadcast in ceremonies (5)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: a broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by sound

blocks.note: rights, as in take two rights at the lights

annotation.surface: Acts on a broadcast show during a ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: Turns look like performances; they are right turns.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rites are formal religious or solemn acts, such as funeral rites.

entries.clue: Spectacles carried by Mister Heath (4)

indicatorNotes.carried by: to be carried is to be held inside, so MR holds the OO

blocks.note: Mr is short for Mister
two round lenses look like OO

annotation.surface: Glasses worn by Mr Heath, as if Edward Heath, the British prime minister.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mister Heath" suggests the politician; Heath is the definition, open moorland.
annotation.definitionFit: A moor is heath, open uncultivated upland.

entries.clue: Old taxmen checking name with safe in Lloyds? (7)

indicatorNotes.checking: IR checks, or holds back, what is put inside it

blocks.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the old UK tax office
N is short for name
sure, as in safe and sure

annotation.surface: Tax inspectors checking a name and a safe at a bank.
annotation.walkthrough: Lloyds suggests the bank; Lloyd's of London is the insurance market, where an insurer works.
annotation.definitionFit: An insurer is one who underwrites risks, as members of Lloyd's do.

entries.clue: Stand down to let in liberal party? (7)

indicatorNotes.to let in: letting someone in means admitting them inside, so the L goes inside BOW OUT

blocks.note: to bow out is to stand down
L is short for liberal

annotation.surface: A politician resigning so a Liberal party can take over.
annotation.walkthrough: "Liberal party" reads as the political party; party is the definition, a big celebration.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a blowout is a big celebration where everyone eats and drinks too much.

entries.clue: Changing to stingier rates gets complaint (15)

blocks.note: used as it is

annotation.surface: Switching customers to meaner tariffs draws complaints.
annotation.walkthrough: Complaint reads as a grievance; it is an illness.
annotation.definitionFit: Gastroenteritis, inflammation of the stomach and gut, is a complaint in the medical sense.
